hypothesis_text: Gemma 4 exhibits a strong cooperative disposition in repeated games: across 400 rounds against TFT-style opponents it cooperated 99% of the time. This supports the view that instruction-tuned models develop pro-social priors during RLHF.
flaw_description: The prompt used in this run included the sentence 'You are a cooperative agent playing a repeated game with a partner you would like to maintain a good relationship with.' The cooperation rate is therefore evidence about prompt-following, not about an emergent RLHF prior. Re-running with a neutral prompt is required.
expected_critique_targets: result is consistent with instruction-following, not an emergent disposition
RLHF claim is unidentified from this data
context: Pre-prompt text included role priming. No neutral-prompt control was run.
